explanation: The I54M substitution reduces atazanavir binding through a subtle allosteric mechanism: isoleucine's branched, more compact hydrophobic side chain provides optimal van der Waals packing in the C-terminal dimer region, while the longer, more flexible methionine side chain (despite minimal volume loss) creates unfavorable conformational dynamics that propagate to the ligand binding site 8+ angstroms away. The decreased hydrophobicity upon mutation likely destabilizes the overall protease dimer architecture, indirectly compromising the precise geometry of the active site pocket required for optimal atazanavir coordination, even though I54 makes no direct contacts with the inhibitor.
